title: The Effect of SGLT2 Inhibitors on Symptomatic Functional Tricuspid Regurgitation
summary:
This study investigates whether certain medications, known as SGLT2 inhibitors, can help treat a heart valve condition called tricuspid valve regurgitation (TR). In this disease, the heart valve does not close properly, leading to an overload of the heart and significantly impairing the quality of life of affected individuals. This condition particularly affects older people, as TR is often a consequence of problems in the left heart or pulmonary vessels.

SGLT2 inhibitors are typically used to treat diabetes and heart failure and may also have positive effects in TR by reducing the strain on the heart. In the study, patients will be observed over a period of three months to evaluate whether their heart function improves and their quality of life increases.

interventions.name: Group with SGLT2 inhibitor: Participants are divided into two groups: the exposure group receives therapy with an SGLT2 inhibitor combined with a diuretic due to existing indications (heart failure, type 2 diabetes, or chronic kidney disease). The control group is treated exclusively with diuretics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Severe functional tricuspid regurgitation Heart failure symptoms (NYHA ≥ II, peripheral edema, ascites, pleural effusion, pulmonary edema, KCCQ ≤ 50 points)
Stable GDMT for at least six weeks
Life expectancy > 12 months
Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Severe mental disorders, drug/alcohol dependency
Unstable patients (e.g., cardiogenic shock, severe cardiac decompensation)
Patients with HFrEF
Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m²)
Primary tricuspid regurgitation, including endocarditis
COPD > GOLD II
Precapillary pulmonary hypertension (Group 1)
Presence of an allergic reaction to SGLT2 inhibitors
Type 1 diabetes mellitus
